metadata.title: PPoPP25-Semi-StructMG-A-Fast-and-Scalable-Semi-Structured-Algebraic-Multigrid-Experiment-Data-and-Source-Codes
metadata.description:
This zenodo repository is for PPoPP 2025 Artifact Evaluation (AE). It contains source codes and data files to reproduce the experiments in the paper. These contents are the same as those of the author's gitee repository (https://gitee.com/zongy17/baseline-recmat). To make the zenodo repository self-contained so that users or readers are easy to access and run, we also include the binary of Semi-StructMG library and the code files of hypre library (recmat branch).

Here is the list of contents:

  • baseline-recmat-master.zip: the code files to call different semi-structured multigrids in solving six test problems (download from https://gitee.com/zongy17/baseline-recmat on Nov 20, 2024)
  • semi-structmg-master.zip: the binary of Semi-StructMG library (download from https://gitee.com/zongy17/semi-struct-mg on Nov 20, 2024)
  • hypre-recmat.zip: the code files of hypre library (recmat branch, download from https://github.com/hypre-space/hypre/tree/recmat on Jan 22, 2024)
  • jsoncpp-1.9.5.zip: a third-party library to process the configuration file input by users of Semi-StructMG (download from https://github.com/open-source-parsers/jsoncpp/tree/1.9.5 on June 7, 2024)
  • oil.tar.gz: binary data of oil reservoir simulation problem
  • kvlcc2.tar.gz: binary data of kvlcc2 ship manufacturing problem
  • gfs.tar.gz:  binary data of global weather forecasting problem
  • ocean.tar.gz: binary data of ocean modeling problem

Note that all these binary data are already in a suitable format for inputting the programs in baseline-recmat-master.zip. To run the experiments, just follow the instructions in its README.md.

metadata.title: Synthesis of Sorting Kernels
metadata.description:
Recently, AlphaDev has shown significant advances in the synthesis of branchless sorting kernels for arrays of lengths $3$ to $5$.
In this paper, we propose an enumerative search technique based on A* search and present novel optimality-pre-serving heuristics and non-optimality-preserving cuts for sorting kernel synthesis.
Our algorithm outperforms AlphaDev in synthesis time by two orders of magnitude ran on a standard notebook instead of a TPU cluster.
Because our algorithm can explore the solution space, we are able to enumerate all correct sorting kernels for length $3$ and simply select the best-performing one.
For larger array lengths, we intelligently sample the solution space and find a sorting kernel that outperforms the state-of-the-art.
Furthermore, we establish a new tight lower bound for the shortest sorting kernel for length $4$.
Finally, we provide a comprehensive comparison against several other existing synthesis techniques and show that none of them is able to synthesize sorting kernels for arrays longer than $3$.

 

This artifact contains the benchmark of the synthesis algorithms and the synthesized kernels' evaluation.

metadata.title: Replication package for: LLMs for Generation of Architectural Components: An Exploratory Empirical Study in the Serverless World
metadata.description: This artifact presents a replication package for the ICSA 2025 submission titled "LLMs for Generation of Architectural Components: An Exploratory Empirical Study in the Serverless World" by Shrikara Arun*, Meghana Tedla*, Karthik Vaidhyanathan (* indicates equal contribution). This project investigates the capabilities of Large Language Models (LLMs) to generate architectural components, specifically focusing on Functions as a Service (FaaS), commonly referred to as serverless functions. By extending the scope of LLM-generated code from snippets to complete architectural components, this work introduces the potential to bridge design decisions directly to deployment, streamlining the software development process. This replication package is applying for the Research Object Reviewed (ROR) ROR-Functional, ROR Reusable and Open Research Object (ORO) badges. We are not applying for Results Validated badges (Results Reproduced (ROR-R) and Results Replicated (RER)) since we do not have independent researchers for verification nor is the reproduction of all results low effort. It involves significant investment in terms of time (execution and person hours) and non-zero cost to generate the serverless functions using the LLMs. This artifact contains the code for the automated steps in our study workflow, including: 1. filtering the Wonderless dataset for presence of tests & sorting based on GitHub stars and forks, 2. creating prompts, codebase summaries and serverless function descriptions using LLMs, 3. generating serverless functions using LLMs, 4. evaluating CodeBLEU and code metrics (LOC, cyclomatic and cognitive complexity and Halstead's volume) and 5. evaluating consistency of LLM generated serverless functions over multiple runs for the metrics previously mentioned. The artifact and instructions can be found at https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.14539783. Support is only provided for AMD64 Linux machines.

metadata.title: Clue Reproduction Artifact - A Comprehensive Experimentation Framework for Energy-Efficient Design of Cloud-Native Applications
metadata.description:
Clue Reproduction Artifact


This is the reproduction artifact for the paper "A Comprehensive Experimentation Framework for Energy-Efficient Design of Cloud-Native Applications" accepted at the 22nd IEEE International Conference on Software Architecture (ICSA 2025), Odense, Denmark. 


This reproduction artifact consists of two parts:

01 Data/
The experimentally obtained data and the analysis scripts used in the paper.

02 Clue/
A snapshot of the clue framework repository used in the paper, and a snapshot of the TeaStore we used in the paper. You can find the latest version of the Clue framework at https://github.com/ISE-TU-Berlin/Clue and https://github.com/ISE-TU-Berlin/sustainable_teastore.

To reproduce the results in the paper, please follow the instructions in the README.md file in each folder and have a look at the Install.md for details about requrimentes.

metadata.title: Analysing Self-Adaptive Systems as Software Product Lines (Artifact)
metadata.description:
This repository contains the implementation of a small-scale evaluation of an autonomous underwater vehicle (AUV) with the mission to find and inspect a pipeline located on a seabed which was inspired by the exemplar SUAVE. The small-scale evaluation was used in a journal paper, recently accepted for publication in the Journal of Systems & Software. A pre-print of the manuscript is included in this repository.
The small-scale evaluation in this repository is an extended version of the small-scale evaluation presented and published at iFM 2023, the paper can be found here. The artifact associated to the iFM 2023 paper was published as an original software publication in Science of Computer Programming, the publication can be found here and the models here or in the `scp-ifm_artifact` branch on GitHub.
 
The goal of this artifact is to show how a self-adaptive system can be modelled and analysed with a probabilistic, feature guarded transition system and a controller switching between features. ProFeat is used as a tool to show this approach. The artifact accompanies the paper "Analysing Self-Adaptive Systems as Software Product Lines", submitted to the special issue on Intelligent Software Product Lines of the Journal of Systems and Software.

The artifact is also available on GitHub.

metadata.title: Mechanized RS274 semantics for additive manufacturing
metadata.description: This artifact contains proof files (.mlw and .v) for a verified interpreter for the RS274/NGC language. The overall verification effort was split into verification of purely modal states and verification of physical states of the machine. Correctness properties of the modal state update was verified in Why3 as .mlw files, and correctness properties of the physical state update was verified using Coq as .v files.

metadata.description:
This is an artifact for the paper "Study of the Use of Property Probes in an Educational Setting".
The artifact contains data related to the interviews and log-file analysis. For example, it contains the following:

Interviews:

  • The coding scheme which was extracted from the interview transcripts.

Log-file analysis:

  • A script used to process the gathered log files into a single csv file.
  • An anonymised version of that csv file.
